kari.docs: Pushed a docs PR adding an 'On‑prem installer troubleshooting' appendix for Private/VPC. Focus: HSM pkcs11 path guidance, minimal egress for semi‑airgapped installs, and short SDK conn‑check snippets. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4999
shawn.eng: Nice. Can you keep the config examples minimal (diff style) and avoid any real hostnames? Also add a short note about exporting key‑wrap metadata before migration.
anika.sec: Security note: explicitly warn never to check in private keys or literal credentials. Add guidance on least‑privilege operator accounts and auditing HSM ACLs.
paul.sre: From SRE: include MTU and NAT hairpin troubleshooting tips for baremetal. Suggest adding a tiny systemd drop‑in example for PKCS11 env when the module is on removable storage. Example below.
paul.sre: ```
# /etc/systemd/system/redwood-hsm.service.d/override.conf
[Service]
Environment=PKCS11_MODULE=/opt/hsm/lib/libpkcs11.so
Restart=on-failure
After=local-fs.target network.target
```
kari.docs: Thanks. I'll add that, plus a compact config diff rather than full config so we don't risk leaking anything. Planning to include Node + Python conn‑check snippets pointing at a private.local host.
shawn.eng: For wording, prefer "configure pkcs11 plugin path via the KMS connector" instead of "open pkcs11". Also add a brief migration caution: test export/import on staging HSM first, then rotate keys during a maintenance window.
anika.sec: Also add a short key‑rotation caveat: snapshot HSM policies before rotation and validate on staging. Remove any literal credentials and use placeholders.
kari.docs: Draft config diff I'll include: ```diff
- kms:
-   type: managed
-   endpoint: https://kms-managed.example
+ kms:
+   type: pkcs11
+   pkcs11_module: /opt/hsm/lib/libpkcs11.so
+   slot: 0
+   label: redwood-kms
```
paul.sre: Add minimal egress CIDRs for conn‑check examples (staging only): 203.0.113.0/24:443, 198.51.100.0/24:443. Note DNS fallback to internal resolver or 1.1.1.1 if allowed. Also include a one‑line troubleshooting command for MTU: `dmesg | grep -i mtu`.
